newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lagardere rises on Thomson-CSF bid hopes.
newsitem.headline: Lagardere rises on Thomson-CSF bid hopes.

text.p: Shares in French missiles-to-publishing group Lagardere rose on Monday, spurred by hopes it could win the bidding on the privatisation of defence electronics company Thomson-CSF.

Traders said newsletter La Lettre de L'Expansion reported the chairmen of Lagardere, Jean-Luc Lagardere, and Alcatel Alsthom, Serge Tchuruk, had met secretly to discuss the Thomson-CSF deal. There were also comments from British Aerospace Plc chairman Sir Richard Evans supporting Lagardere's bid, published last week.
Lagardere was up 2.62 percent at 172.4 at 1110 GMT.
The French government wants rivals Alcatel and Lagadere to join forces in bidding for Thomson-CSF, which would make a French national champion to confront the U.S. competition.

But last Thursday, in an interview with Le Monde, BAe's Evans said his company supports Lagardere's bid and if a purely nationalist approach were taken in the French defence industry restructuring, BAe would look to moving closer to GEC Plc and Daimler-Benz Aerospace.
La Lettre de l'Expansion said, "The head of Matra (Lagardere), who knows that he remains the favourite among bookmakers, is naturally tempted to offer a consolation prize to his challenger Alcatel.
"But a dialogue of the deaf is sure. Tchuruk is not a man to be satisfied with second place," the newsletter said.
